newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. denies clemency to condemned murderer.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. denies clemency to condemned murderer.

text.p: Gov. Pete Wilson Thursday denied clemency to a convicted rapist and murderer who is set to be executed next week despite his pleas of innocence.

Thomas Thompson, 42, who is scheduled to be put to death by lethal injection at San Quentin State Prison early next Tuesday, was sentenced to death for the 1981 rape and murder of Ginger Fleischli, 20, in Laguna Beach, southern California.
He would be the fifth person executed in California since the state resumed executions in 1992.

"Ginger Fleischli's death sentence arrived within hours of her encounter with Mr. Thompson on September 11, 1981. By contrast, Mr. Thompson has had more than 16 years of life since he committed the ultimate crime. I will not stand in the way of his ultimate punishment," Wilson said in a statement announcing he was denying clemency.
Thompson's lawyers, citing new evidence, petitioned Wilson to reduce his death sentence to one of life imprisonment without possibility of parole.
Thompson has consistently maintained he is innocent.
He has stated that after an evening of drinking and smoking hashish, he and Fleischli had consensual sex at a Laguna Beach apartment after which he passed out.
Her body was found a few days later in a shallow grave. Her shirt and bra had been cut in front and pulled down to her elbows. Investigators found the victim's blood on the carpet of the apartment.
Thompson's roommate David Leitch was convicted of second-degree murder for aiding in Fleischli's death and was sentenced to 15 years to life imprisonment.
At a recent clemency hearing, Thompson's lawyers cited Leitch's testimony at a 1995 parole hearing suggesting that he saw Thompson and Fleischli having consensual sex.
Thompson was eligible for the death penalty for the murder because he was also convicted of rape which is a "special circumstance" under California law.

In his written decision, Wilson, a Republican known for a tough stance on law and order, said that Thompson's claim of innocence was based on "the inherently incredible alibi" that Thompson slept through the murder.
Thompson has another chance to avoid execution.
A federal appeals court in San Francisco has agreed to hold a hearing Friday to decide whether it would be a "fundamental miscarriage of justice" to let Thompson be put to death.
